intent: Stop the superpowers bookkeeping tree from silently regrowing to the 695 files that made a 655-file prune necessary, by capping it in the gate instead of leaving a note recommending it.
scope: meta/scripts/check_repo_size.sh - adds a per-directory artifact cap
Non-goal: changing the source-file ceiling or the excluded prefixes, both unchanged.
changes: Added ARTIFACT_DIRS + MAX_ARTIFACTS_PER_DIR=60, checked by a new check_artifact_dirs helper wired into main alongside the existing source-file ceiling.
main now accumulates failures rather than returning on the first, so a commit that trips both the source ceiling and the artifact cap reports both.
60 is the headroom the prune bought (21 files per dir today). The header says to prune rather than raise it when it fails.

verification.evidence: '1050 source files (ceiling 1200)' EXIT=0 with evidence/contracts at 21 each, under the 60 cap. --count still prints the bare number, EXIT=0.
EXIT=1 listing BOTH dirs (evidence 22, contracts 21) plus the prune hint - confirms the new branch fires and that it does not stop at the first offender.

verification.command: pre-commit run repo-size-cap --all-files; pre-commit run --files meta/scripts/check_repo_size.sh
verification.evidence: Hook Passed; shfmt and shellcheck clean on the modified script.

risks: A legitimate burst of commits can now trip the cap and block a commit until artifacts are pruned. That is the intended trade: the previous behaviour was unbounded growth noticed only months later.
The cap counts tracked files per directory, so it does not distinguish a needed recent artifact from an old one; the operator chooses what to prune.
rollback: git revert the commit; the source-file ceiling and all other behaviour are untouched by this change.
After rollback, confirm ./meta/scripts/check_repo_size.sh still exits 0 and prints the source count.
